_note: Every fact below was read on the NASA page named in source_url on verified_on. Anything not on a page was left out. 'game' fields mark simplifications.

water90.text: The space station reclaims about 90% of the water its crew uses, including urine, sweat and breath moisture.

bone1.text: Without precautions, an astronaut's weight-bearing bones become roughly 1% less dense for every month in space.

exercise2h.text: Space station crews exercise for an average of two hours a day to protect their bones and muscles.

moxie6.text: MOXIE on the Perseverance rover made oxygen from Mars air. Its design goal was 6 grams per hour, and it reached nearly 10.56 grams per hour at peak.

dustPanels.text: Cleaning dusty solar panels to keep power up could be a very real job for future human explorers on Mars.

dustOpportunity.text: In 2018 a dust storm that circled Mars blotted out the sunlight that the solar-powered Opportunity rover needs. The nuclear-powered Curiosity rover was largely unaffected.

commsDelay.text: A message between Earth and Mars takes about 4 minutes one way when the planets are closest and about 24 minutes when they are farthest apart.

gravityMars.text: Gravity on the surface of Mars is 3.73 m/s2, which is 0.38 times Earth's.

gravityMoon.text: Gravity on the surface of the Moon is 1.62 m/s2, which is 0.165 times Earth's.

flareScale.text: Each step up the flare class scale (C, M, X) is ten times stronger: an X flare is 10 times an M and 100 times a C.
flareScale.verified_how: Read in a search-result excerpt of the NASA SVS page and the GOES X-ray description page. The pages themselves could not be fetched from this network, so this one is only partly verified.
